thesis: The discussion argues that effective risk management requires balancing the pursuit of profit with the ability to act as a risk manager, emphasizing contingency planning over the ability to predict the future. It further asserts that successful leadership during a crisis depends on preparation, judgment, and the capacity to act decisively when information is incomplete, noting that one should seek board members who have already experienced a crisis rather than relying on appearances.
